title: Sailing Performance vs Polars
dataSources: NMEA/SignalK data (`nmea:reading`), bilge pump (`bilge:event`), mooring/anchor watch (`mooring:status`), marine weather (`marineweather:forecast`).
app: Marine electronics — NMEA 2000 / SignalK boat networks, bilge, battery and shore-power sensors, anchor-watch GPS, and marine weather feeds — streamed to Splunk HEC via SignalK and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=nmea:reading measurement=sailing
| eval polar_pct=round(100*boatspeed_kt/target_speed_kt,1)
| bin _time span=10min
| stats avg(polar_pct) as performance by _time
| sort - _time
description: Compares your boat speed against its theoretical polar targets for the wind, measuring how well you are trimmed.
value: Sailing to polars is how racers extract speed; a live performance percentage guides trim and course choices.
implementation: Ingest speed and wind data into `index=personal`; compute performance against polar targets.
visualization: Line chart of sailing performance versus polar targets.
grandmaExplanation: It compares your boat's speed to its ideal for the wind, showing how well the sails are trimmed.
